Senses.Note: The apparent definition-form hit for ‘face + one who’ (面門者) is not a definition: it occurs inside ‘how many people have split open the face?’ (󳮢破面門者幾人), where the final graph marks the person performing the verb. The inventory likewise found ‘the so-called face, nostrils, ears, eyes, heels, and brains’ (所謂面門、鼻孔、耳朵、眼睛、腳跟、頭腦), an enumeration rather than a gloss. The Linji occurrence is a raised case under Vinaya Master Bensong's section of the Five Lamps Compendium; Linji Yixuan remains the exact quoted utterer and Bensong the later raiser.

Senses.Explanation: The face or face-front: a bodily front imagined as a gate or opening. The graphs join 'face' (面) to 'gate or opening' (門), and the compound has 1,040 occurrences in 287 allowlisted texts. Its physical reference is explicit when Baozhi uses a finger to split open his face (以指𠢐面門) and when a fire-mass is said to scorch the face of anyone who comes near (近著即燎却面門). The record also uses verbs of impact with it: ‘press through the face’ (拶破面門) has 42 occurrences in 34 texts, while ‘scorch the face’ (燎却面門) has 53 in 34. In the repeatedly quoted Linji case, ‘the true person of no rank’ (無位真人) is said to be constantly entering and leaving through the faces of the people present (常在汝等諸人面門出入); ‘entering and leaving through the face’ (面門出入) occurs 246 times in 157 storage files representing 154 independent works. Yuanwu also records ‘a dynamic at the face’ (面門一機) in a small address and tells his interlocutor that he remains unaware even when it has ‘pressed through his face’ (拶破面門). These are the attested bodily, spatial, and case-specific uses; the texts do not supply a separate abstract definition for the compound.
